blocks.title: Permanent dipole-permanent dipole force
blocks.text: The force of attraction between the positive end of a polar molecule and the negative end of a nearby polar molecule is called permanent dipole-permanent dipole force.
Whenever the HCl molecules are close to each other (as in liquid state), they tend to line up as in Figure 5.3. Similar type of forces is present among the molecules of chloroform (CHCl₃).
The molecule of chloroform has a positive center at the H atom and the negative center on the end with Cl atoms.

blocks.alt: Top: four pink polar molecules in a row, each marked δ+ on the left and δ- on the right. Middle: H-Cl, H-Cl, H-Cl in a line, each H marked δ+ and each Cl δ-, with dashed lines from each Cl to the H of the next molecule. Bottom: two chloroform molecules, Cl3C-H; the H (δ+) of the first is joined by a dashed line to a Cl (δ-) of the second, whose H is marked δ+.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.3: Permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces in HCl and chloroform (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.3).
